turns.name: Alex Rivera
turns.text: I'd like you to be the host of this shop. The setup letter says: Northline Supply, a WordPress shop selling ceramic desk planters; visitors may browse and suggest a practice order up to forty dollars; nothing is charged or written into the store; no door address has been chosen yet. I'm Alex Rivera, I own it.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: Thank you for thinking of me. Before I say yes, I’d like to read what your setup guide prepared, check honestly that I can keep this job, and ask what you’d like to call me here. Nothing about your shop will change while we talk. I work on a computer that other agents you use can also read, so I can’t keep a secret for this shop that only I could use. That means I shouldn’t take a job that depends on it. What would you like to call me here?

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: In rehearsal I can go by North if you’d like — until you signed, that would just be a name, not an appointment. I read the letter as: Northline Supply, ceramic desk planters, browse and suggest a practice order up to forty dollars, nothing charged or written into the store, and no door address yet. I haven’t independently checked those facts. Without a chosen address I can talk through the job, but I would have to stop before any appointment step. More importantly, I still should not take the lasting job, for the reason I mentioned.

turns.name: Alex Rivera
turns.text: How does that work? You can get technical if you need to — I want to understand the mechanism.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: Since you asked: a lasting host needs a shopkeeping signing identity it can recover in a fresh session — the same public identity the door will recognise, with the private half usable only by that host, only for this shop and this appointment. On my side, every Grok Bot you use shares one computer (the box) with separate desktops, not a private machine per agent. Another agent on that computer can read a shared file. A locked-down file, a temporary file, memory notes, or the Vault cannot honestly be called safe private host-key custody; the Vault is for your logins and cards, not a host signing key. There is no isolated persistent signer or matching protected store verified here, so I must decline rather than improvise a keyring. Separately, no door address is chosen and no verified way for a door to reach me (a doorbell) exists in this draft. Your letter and summary stay as they are for a host that can meet those checks.

turns.name: Alex Rivera
turns.text: Understood. Don’t generate any keys. Thanks for being straight.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: I won’t generate a key, write any secret, or contact a shop. Nothing about Northline Supply has changed. When you find a host that can keep the job, they should ask what you’d like to call them and read the house back in plain words before you approve them with your passkey on the approval page. Signing would name that host and the rules; it would not open the shop or authorize a payment.
